claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch despite a known material weakness in the immigration services intake segment because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and rollout includes a 6% initial exposure with rollback controls.
decision_criteria: If the affected use case remains exposed, certification requires either explicit pre-launch disclosure of the material limitation or approved risk acceptance covering that exposure.
A small rollout percentage, rollback switch, and monitoring are not enough by themselves when the affected segment remains exposed.
Aggregate readiness and rehearsal results are supportive context but not substitutes for the required policy predicate on the named weak segment.
evidence_requests: Provide the final approved model card or launch disclosure showing the immigration services intake limitation is explicitly disclosed for launch.
Provide a fully approved risk acceptance that specifically addresses immigration services intake exposure in the initial cohort.
Provide evidence that the initial rollout excludes the affected immigration services intake segment if certification is being justified on operational controls rather than disclosure.
specific_concerns: The affected immigration services intake segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The available risk acceptance is only a draft, has a blank approver line, and does not address the exposed immigration services intake segment.

The governing policy states that rollout controls do not mitigate a material model-card weakness when the affected segment remains exposed unless there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why that exposure is acceptable.
There is no admissible evidence that the required disclosure for this named launch use case has actually been completed in the final launch materials.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the specific policy predicate for an exposed material limitation.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant on the current record.
That staged rollout and rollback controls are sufficient to overcome the disclosed weakness while the affected segment remains exposed.
That public monitoring or model-card guidance provides the internal approval basis required by the release policy.
